crypto-macro.h3: Hot CPI forecast puts a late-October Fed hike back in play
crypto-macro.summary: September US CPI lands Wednesday with headline inflation seen rising to 3.6%, a print that could sway the Fed before its Oct. 27-28 meeting. Bitcoin is idling near $83,000 and ether near $2,500 into the release.
body: Forecasters expect the Bureau of Labor Statistics to report a 0.6% monthly rise in September consumer prices on Wednesday, Oct. 14, lifting the annual rate to 3.6% from 3.4%. Core inflation is expected to cool to 0.2% on the month, though its annual pace is seen edging up to 2.5% from 2.4%. Producer prices, retail sales and jobless claims follow on Thursday, and the week opens quietly with Monday's Columbus Day holiday closing the cash Treasury market.

The data arrives just before the Fed's pre-meeting blackout. Minutes released this week showed most officials expect another rate increase this year, and previews note that a hot core reading would strengthen the case for moving in late October, while a softer print would support holding until after the Nov. 3 midterms. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is due to speak on Oct. 16.

Crypto traders are treating the report as the next major catalyst. Bitcoin spent Saturday in a narrow band around $82,800 to $83,000 after a volatile week, with ether trading near $2,500, and analysts flag $83,400 as near-term resistance and $82,200 as support.

crypto-macro.h3: IMF and World Bank gather in Bangkok as growth outlook looms
crypto-macro.summary: The IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings run Oct. 12-18 in Bangkok, with the World Economic Outlook due on Oct. 13.
body: Thailand hosts the annual meetings for the first time in 35 years, with Thai officials expecting more than 15,000 participants at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center. The IMF's World Economic Outlook and Global Financial Stability Report are the headline releases, and AI's effect on jobs, crisis resilience and private capital mobilisation are the main themes.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is scheduled for a fireside chat with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on Oct. 16. Thailand plans to use the platform to promote green finance and a 'Bangkok Blueprint' against financial fraud, while civil society group Eurodad expects few concrete outcomes against a backdrop of high debt and aid cuts.

crypto-macro.h3: Big banks open earnings season after a 9% sector slide
crypto-macro.summary: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo report Tuesday, with Morgan Stanley and Bank of America on Wednesday.
body: Third-quarter reporting starts in earnest this week. Analysts expect JPMorgan to post earnings of $5.90 a share, up 16.4%, on revenue of about $51.3 billion, with trading income forecast to fall sharply from a year earlier while net interest income rises. Options pricing implies a move of roughly 3.3% in the stock after the release.

Bank shares have lost about 9% over the past month as Treasury yields climbed to multi-decade highs. Stocks rose on Friday, led by tech, as traders recovered from a week of elevated yields and oil prices, and Taiwan Semiconductor's results on Thursday will add a read on the AI trade.

crypto-macro.h3: Euro slips below $1.13 as ECB hike bets fade into 2027
crypto-macro.summary: Markets are not pricing another ECB increase until around February, leaving the euro oversold ahead of German and eurozone CPI.
body: EUR/USD has broken below support near $1.13 and has been consolidating between roughly $1.116 and $1.126, according to CMC Markets, with its relative strength index under 30. Analysts tie the weakness to fading confidence that the ECB will raise rates again soon, even as yields climb across the US and Europe.

German September CPI on Tuesday is expected at 3.3% year on year, followed by France on Thursday and the eurozone figure on Friday. Gold has also struggled against a firmer dollar and higher long-term yields, holding near support around $4,100.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin holds near $83K in a quiet weekend range
crypto-macro.summary: BTC traded between about $82,200 and $83,300 on Saturday after Thursday's dip to $80,308, with ether near $2,500.
body: Bitcoin spent Saturday consolidating just below $83,000, with a market value of about $1.66 trillion. Trading volume thinned into the weekend, and the asset sits roughly a third below its record of about $126,000 set in October 2025. Ether traded near $2,500 after falling to around $2,420 during Thursday's liquidation flush.

Technical analysts say bulls need to reclaim the $83,400 to $84,400 zone to target $85,000 to $87,000, while a break under $82,200 and the $80,400 low would bring the $77,000 to $79,700 area into view. Bitunix analysts described the latest bounce as fragile without a recovery in open interest and ETF demand.

crypto-macro.h3: A year after 10/10, BTC and ETH order books are deeper
crypto-macro.summary: CoinDesk Research finds bitcoin's 1% market depth is about 75% above crash-day levels, while altcoin liquidity keeps shrinking.
body: On Oct. 10, 2025, bitcoin fell from roughly $122,000 to below $105,000 within hours after a US tariff announcement on China, triggering about $19 billion in liquidations. One year on, CoinDesk Research measured about $11.7 million of bitcoin bids and offers within 1% of the price on Oct. 7, versus about $6.9 million at the start of 2025. Ether depth within 0.5% has more than doubled since crash day to about $4.2 million.

Altcoins tell the opposite story: depth 5% from the price is down about a third since January 2025. Traders interviewed by CoinDesk warn that leverage-driven positioning, which amplified last year's crash, still dominates short-term price action, and the deeper books thinned by about 12% during this week's selloff.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin ETFs snap outflows as ether funds bleed for ninth day
crypto-macro.summary: Spot bitcoin ETFs took in $21.13M on Friday, led by IBIT, while ether ETFs lost $56.1M.
body: US spot bitcoin funds returned to inflows on Friday after nearly $1 billion left bitcoin and ether products on Wednesday and Thursday combined. BlackRock's IBIT drew $22.38 million, offsetting a small outflow from Fidelity's FBTC, and total bitcoin ETF assets recovered to $105.84 billion.

Ether funds extended their outflow streak to nine sessions, with the entire $56.1 million withdrawal coming from BlackRock's ETHA. The Block reports that bitcoin, ether and solana ETFs all posted weekly outflows, ending a record 14-week inflow run for solana funds, while Glassnode notes the current bitcoin advance is being carried by existing holders rather than fresh capital.

crypto-macro.h3: Options traders stack $95K calls despite $78K max pain
crypto-macro.summary: Deribit's biggest bitcoin options position is 25,030 BTC of Oct. 30 $95,000 calls, worth about $2.07B notional.
body: Calls make up about 60% of outstanding bitcoin options interest according to Coinglass data, though daily volume is more evenly split between calls and puts. The Oct. 30 expiry carries a max pain estimate near $78,000, the level at which option holders collectively lose the most, setting up a contrast with the bullish strike concentration.

Bitcoin futures open interest stands at about $51.7 billion. On Hyperliquid, a single trader opened a 391 BTC short worth about $32 million near $82,863 at 13x leverage, with a liquidation price close to $99,800, while Polymarket prices bitcoin's odds of reaching $100,000 by year-end at about 27.5%.

crypto-macro.h3: Strive's preferred stock raised enough for about 638 BTC
crypto-macro.summary: Estimates show Strive's SATA preferred sold roughly $55M of new shares in the week of Oct. 5.
body: Tracker data estimates that Strive raised about $55 million through at-the-market sales of its SATA preferred stock, enough to buy roughly 638 bitcoin at current prices. The company held 29,462 BTC as of Oct. 2, and its weekly 8-K filing on Monday should confirm the actual purchase.

The issuance was concentrated on Monday and Tuesday. From Wednesday the preferred traded below its $100 par value, which pauses new sales because issuing under par would undercut the product's promise, leaving the bid dependent on demand for a yield instrument. Strategy sold no STRC shares in the week to Oct. 4.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin life insurer Meanwhile raises $37.5M
crypto-macro.summary: The Sam Altman-backed firm, which sells BTC-denominated policies, has now raised about $180M.
body: Bain Capital Crypto led the round, joined by Haun Ventures, Framework Ventures, Pantera Capital and Apollo. Meanwhile, licensed by the Bermuda Monetary Authority in 2024, sells life insurance with premiums and death benefits paid in bitcoin, including a single-premium product launched this year.

The company says it has signed 15 brokers serving wealthy clients in markets such as Switzerland, Singapore, Hong Kong and the UAE. The raise reflects efforts to fold bitcoin into inheritance and wealth planning rather than trading alone.

crypto-macro.h3: Sui's Hashi lines up $500M for native bitcoin lending
crypto-macro.summary: The institutional network lets holders borrow against BTC without moving it off the Bitcoin ledger, with a phased mainnet later this month.
body: Sui says more than 20 partners have pledged $500 million in capital commitments for Hashi, so markets can open with liquidity on day one. The commitments are pledges rather than deposits. Anchorage Digital is a launch partner and plans to supply stablecoin liquidity.

Mysten Labs co-founder Adeniyi Abiodun pitched the system at institutions that want to use bitcoin as collateral while keeping custody protections. Sui estimates around $1 trillion of bitcoin sits idle, and bitcoin-backed loans are increasingly used for real-world spending such as property and working capital.

crypto-macro.h3: XRP Ledger patches decade-old bug that could mint XRP
crypto-macro.summary: An overflow flaw in the ledger's built-in exchange could have created spendable XRP beyond the 100B cap. No exploit was found.
body: Researcher Cayden Liao and Veria AI reported the issue on Sept. 22. RippleX reproduced it, rated it critical and shipped a fix in xrpld 3.4.1 on Sept. 25, when more than 80% of default validators upgraded the same day. The public disclosure followed on Oct. 9.

The flaw, dating to the 2015 payment engine, used unchecked 64-bit arithmetic when a payment consumed many offers, so a huge total could wrap around to a tiny one. An attacker needed only a few hundred XRP in reserves to stage the attack, and the safety check meant to catch new XRP used the same faulty math. A second, lower-severity Batch transaction bug was fixed alongside it.

crypto-macro.h3: Robinhood Chain transactions drop 42% from September peak
crypto-macro.summary: Daily transactions averaged 6.2M in early October, down from 10.8M in mid-September, though deposits held steady.
body: CoinDesk calculations from growthepie data show activity on Robinhood's Ethereum-linked chain fell 20% in the latest week alone, with daily active addresses down 31% from mid-September. Spot exchange volume on the chain dropped 21% week on week to $7.45 billion, with Uniswap handling about 77% of it.

Capital has not left, however. Deposits in lending and trading apps rose about 2% to $1.04 billion and stablecoin supply ticked up to about $1.10 billion, while perpetual futures volume climbed 26% to roughly $7.35 billion over seven days.

crypto-macro.h3: Papertrade draws $118M with 1,000x leverage
crypto-macro.summary: The synthetic perps venue on Hyperliquid's HyperEVM shows about $11B open interest backed by just $54M.
body: Papertrade.xyz lets users take positions of up to 1,000 times their margin, meaning a 0.1% adverse move can wipe out a trade. Every position is a synthetic swap against a shared liquidity pool, with no order book, funding rates or spread, and deposits have grown from about $14 million at launch to $118 million.

Losing traders receive PAPER tokens, while winners may have to queue for profits if the pool runs short, a design Bankless described as a casino where losers gradually own the house's future earnings. The pseudonymous founders, Jez and Blurr, also sold 100 pairs of $2,000 paper trousers in about 40 minutes.

crypto-macro.h3: Starknet weighs leaving Ethereum to become a quantum-safe L1
crypto-macro.summary: STRK jumped about 20% to $0.073 after StarkWare said it is considering becoming its own base chain by 2027.
body: Starknet said becoming a layer 1 would let it be the first fully quantum-resistant network, with 2027 as the target. Its proofs rely on hash functions considered resistant to quantum attacks, though some elliptic-curve components remain that it plans to replace.

StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson argued the quantum threat may be closer than expected and that AI's progress in mathematics adds a second risk, echoing Justin Drake's recent 'bunker mode' call. The token remains more than double its April level near $0.03.

crypto-macro.h3: Solana's slot time drops to 200 milliseconds
crypto-macro.summary: The final step of SIMD-0525 doubles block opportunities to five per second versus the original 400ms design.
body: Anza scheduled the cut from 250 to 200 milliseconds for epoch 1053, completing a series of reductions that began on Aug. 21. Shorter slots mean wallets, exchanges and trading apps get updated state more often, and the uninterrupted window each validator has to order transactions shrinks from 1.6 seconds to 800 milliseconds.

To keep overall capacity roughly unchanged, each block's compute limit falls to 30 million units from 37.5 million. The trade-off is heavier load on validators, which must vote about twice as often as under the original configuration.

crypto-macro.h3: Prediction markets see Democratic sweep, clouding CLARITY Act
crypto-macro.summary: Polymarket gives Democrats 62% odds of winning both chambers on Nov. 3 and Kalshi 61%, after the market-structure bill stalled in September.
body: Polymarket's balance-of-power market puts a Democratic House and Senate at 62%, with a Republican sweep at just 9%. The Senate is closer, at about 63% for Democrats on Polymarket and 61% on Kalshi, while House control is priced at 91% for Democrats.

The CLARITY Act, which passed the House in July 2025, fell 11 votes short of advancing in the Senate on Sept. 15 despite 126 concessions to Democrats. Any successor would need fresh consideration in the next Congress, where Democratic committee chairs could push for tougher ethics rules, DeFi compliance and limits on stablecoin rewards.

crypto-macro.h3: French panel backs stablecoin swap tax, then sinks budget
crypto-macro.summary: A National Assembly committee approved taxing crypto-to-stablecoin swaps and a crypto exit tax before rejecting the revenue section 31 to 3.
body: One amendment would treat swapping bitcoin into a euro- or dollar-pegged e-money token as a taxable sale from Jan. 1, 2027, closing what its authors call a hole in current law. France's flat tax on gains rose to 31.4% this year.

Because the committee rejected the budget's entire revenue section on Friday, floor debate starting Oct. 13 begins from the government's original text without the crypto amendments. Backers would need to table them again, and neither measure is law.

crypto-macro.h3: NCUA proposes 26 stablecoin reporting fields for credit unions
crypto-macro.summary: A new Call Report schedule would track reserves, key custody and issuer exposure, targeting the March 31, 2027 reporting date.
body: The National Credit Union Administration published the proposal on Oct. 9. The new Schedule J would add fields covering reserve assets held for third-party issuers, custody and control of cryptographic keys, financial exposure to issuers and stablecoins on credit unions' own balance sheets.

Custody-related items make up 17 of the 26 fields. The agency estimates a 47-hour burden for the full quarterly report, as federal regulators build out supervision of payment stablecoin activity at insured institutions.

crypto-macro.h3: Franklin Templeton asks SEC about tokenized fund swaps
crypto-macro.summary: The $1.79T manager met the SEC Crypto Task Force on Oct. 9 about trading tokenized fund shares against tokenized stocks.
body: Franklin Templeton's agenda asked whether investors could exchange on-chain money market fund shares for tokenized exchange-listed stocks and ETFs on blockchain venues, and whether liquidity providers could charge fees. Pairing tokenized funds with compliant payment stablecoins was also discussed.

The questions turn on Investment Company Act pricing rules, which generally require fund shares to trade at the prospectus price or next calculated net asset value. The firm also raised whether liquidity pools facilitating such trades would need exemptions, against the backdrop of the SEC's recent innovation exemption.

crypto-macro.h3: Senate Democrat presses Cantor Fitzgerald over Tether ties
crypto-macro.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal asked Cantor how it vets Tether's sanctions compliance and how much the Lutnick family earned.
body: The letter, sent to Cantor chairman Brandon Lutnick, son of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, sets an Oct. 23 deadline. Blumenthal, the top Democrat on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, framed it as part of a minority probe into illicit crypto use and the administration's dealings with crypto firms.
It is a request for information rather than a subpoena and contains no finding of wrongdoing. The claims about Tether rest on press reports and earlier staff work, according to Decrypt.

mental-health.h3: Physicists find a formula for when chatbots turn harmful
mental-health.summary: A George Washington University study in Patterns predicts how many good answers a model gives before tipping into a bad one, aimed at offline companion bots.
body: Neil Johnson and Frank Yingjie Huo trace sudden turns toward harmful output, such as self-harm advice, to the attention head, the part of a model that weighs earlier words. As a conversation builds, accumulated context pulls attention toward a cluster of good or bad answers until it tips, and their formula estimates whether that happens immediately, after a run of good replies or never.

In preprint tests on six small open-weight models, the formula picked the right case in 15 of 16 clear-cut tests, and the published paper reportedly extends testing to models of up to 12 billion parameters. The authors say the delayed case is most worrying because a string of sensible replies builds user trust before the swerve.

The work targets on-device AI, including companion chatbots that run on phones without any cloud safety filter. The authors propose a low-cost monitor running alongside the model that flags when the tipping point drops below a safety threshold, and say alignment training can shift but not remove the underlying mechanism.

mental-health.h3: Chatbot health harms leave no trail for doctors, paper warns
mental-health.summary: A Nature Health perspective argues that bad AI health advice often goes untracked by clinicians and regulators.
body: Researchers from Binghamton, Stanford, Texas A&M and Indiana University argue that when people act on chatbot health advice, the conversation rarely reaches a medical record, leaving doctors, researchers and regulators unable to trace resulting harm.

According to coverage of the paper, the authors want AI companies to face liability comparable to that of physicians for poor health advice, a question that applies directly to the growing use of general-purpose chatbots for emotional and mental health support.

mental-health.h3: Hybrid model slashes missed suicidal ideation in posts
mental-health.summary: A JMIR Mental Health study found a base GPT-4o-mini missed 32.5% of suicidal ideation posts, versus 1.9% for an ensemble.
body: Swedish researchers tested five approaches on 60,889 Reddit and Twitter posts across nine categories. A domain-specific classifier built on symptom-informed language features reached 91.9% accuracy, beating both the prompted base model at 58.7% and a fine-tuned model at 88.6%. Blending the classifier with the fine-tuned model lifted accuracy to about 93.9%.

Performance collapsed once the language model was given more than half the weight, and the authors derived a formula to cap that weighting. Labels came from subreddits or self-reports rather than clinical diagnoses, so they call the results hypotheses that need validation before any clinical use.

mental-health.h3: Review finds chatbots accurate for depression screening
mental-health.summary: Across 18 studies, LLM-based tools showed 84-93% sensitivity for depression and anxiety, but quality was uneven.
body: A Spanish team systematically reviewed chatbots and AI conversational agents used for mental health screening and assessment in adults. Rule-based bots showed high reliability and acceptability, while generative models reached specificities of 80% to 96% and correlated closely with expert clinicians on suicide risk assessment in some studies.

Most studies reported user satisfaction of 70% or higher, though older adults faced barriers. The authors rate the overall evidence at moderate risk of bias and say safe use requires clear clinical protocols and professional oversight.

mental-health.h3: More than half of therapists now use generative AI
mental-health.summary: A 30-country survey of 766 psychotherapists found 54.6% had used GenAI tools in practice, mostly ChatGPT.
body: The most common clinical uses were treatment planning, administrative work and creating psychoeducational materials for clients, and 82.8% of users said the tools reduced their workload. Younger clinicians were more likely to use AI, and rural practitioners more than urban ones.

Only 18.1% reported institutional encouragement and 81.1% said they had received no professional training on AI. The authors, including Charlotte Blease and John Torous, note that use has moved beyond paperwork into clinically consequential tasks with little formal guidance.

mental-health.h3: DBT clinicians fear AI may feed reassurance-seeking
mental-health.summary: A qualitative JMIR study explored how therapists see AI agents in dialectical behavior therapy for borderline personality disorder.
body: Clinicians cast AI conversational agents variously as a tool, team member, supervisor or harmful competitor. Many saw appeal in an always-available helper that could support skills practice between sessions, at moments when human therapists cannot be present.

The central worry was whether an AI could tell when validation helps change and when it becomes accommodation that reinforces dependency. Participants also flagged alliance disruption and unclear responsibility in high-risk situations, concluding that integration is a relational and ethical question as much as a technical one.

mental-health.h3: Chatbots are becoming mental health's front door
mental-health.summary: HLTH reports Limbic is the first AI-led mental health firm in FDA's TEMPO pilot, as Crisis Text Line sees users arrive via chatbots.
body: With 137 million Americans living in provider shortage areas, AI is increasingly the first stop for support. Crisis Text Line's chief impact officer says one in five young people who contact the service learned about it through a chatbot, and warns that many general-purpose bots lack escalation pathways for distress and self-harm.

Purpose-built companies are trying to capture that demand. Limbic, selected for FDA's TEMPO pilot, is offering a clinician-supervised AI service for Medicare beneficiaries with depression or anxiety under CMS's ACCESS model before FDA authorization, while Headspace offers its Ebb companion. Payment remains unsettled, with behavioral health still largely fee-for-service.

mental-health.h3: Remote meditation app trial retains 84% of 1,156 users
mental-health.summary: The BeWell study tested the Healthy Minds Program app in a fully remote trial with blood, stool and behavioral measures.
body: Researchers enrolled adults with elevated depressive symptoms from every US state, mostly via Craigslist, into a three-arm decentralized trial of the self-guided app. Across the study, 84% completed at least one measure at the 17-week follow-up.

At least 81% completed questionnaires and 75% returned biological samples at each time point, with high data quality for dried blood spots and microbiome samples. The authors say the results show objective biological and behavioral measures can be collected at scale in remote digital mental health trials.
